books.name: Genesis
books.executive: Two commits and thirty-nine days of silence between them: a scaffold that named itself Day 1, and a pipeline that arrived carrying the physics of the world it was built for.

strategic.left: Nothing yet. The only thing on the ground was a template: Next.js, Prisma, a magic link, and Tailwind, which the next book carries out.
strategic.taken: A noun before a verb. The Receipt was a table in the first schema before there was any decision to put in it, and the compass, the Y-gate, and WORLD.md arrived to give it something to record.
strategic.seam: Thirty-nine days with no commits. The record shows that work happened in them and not what it was.

operational: The first commit on main is 471d5739, at 11:39 on the morning of 9 April 2026. Its subject calls it Day 1. The status page counts differently: on 29 September it reads DAY 173, which only works if 9 April is Day 0. The world began on a disagreement about where to start counting, and both counts are in the record.

What the scaffold contains is plain. Next.js 16, Prisma 7, Auth.js with a magic link. A schema with a User, a Receipt, and an Outcome. A proxy that guards two routes and sends everyone else to /compass. A package manifest that pulls in Tailwind, which the next book will have to carry out. The commit message ends with a done-state rather than a boast: fill the environment file, migrate, click the link, arrive at /dashboard with a session.

Then the record goes quiet. Between 471d5739 and a61d492e there are no commits on main at all. Thirty-nine days. It would be easy to fill that silence with a story. The Chronicle does not, and the reason is written into the second commit itself.

a61d492e lands on 18 May at 13:32. It carries two database migrations whose own folder names are timestamps: 20260410143234 and 20260410143652, the afternoon of 10 April, the day after Day 0. The work was being done. It was not being committed. The pipeline, the Y-gate, the brief, the guide, and a 188-line WORLD.md all arrive together, thirty-one files and 5,762 lines in one breath, authored from a different address than the first commit.

Before any of it, there is an older book. ADR-071 and the apex-spine canon cite a Book of ARCS from November 2025 as the earliest artifact, the place where three was first named the minimum for coherence. It is not in this repository's history, so this Chronicle cannot prove it. It is cited here as what came before, and marked as such.

claims.text: The first commit on main is 471d5739, dated 2026-04-09 11:39, subject 'Day 1 scaffold'.
status.arcs.care reads DAY 173 on 2026-09-29, which counts 2026-04-09 as Day 0.
The Day 1 schema declares User, Receipt, and Outcome; the scaffold depends on tailwindcss ^4.
No commits exist on main between 471d5739 and a61d492e.
a61d492e adds WORLD.md (188 lines) across 31 files and 5,762 insertions, under a different author email than 471d5739.
What happened in the 39 uncommitted days, beyond the two migration timestamps.
A Book of ARCS existed in November 2025 and named three as the minimum for coherence.

shavasana.release: Released: any reading of the 39 days as idleness. The migration timestamps say work happened; they do not say what or how much, so the Chronicle keeps only the timestamps. Kept: every claim with a sha. Downgraded to unproven: the November 2025 book, which is cited by the canon but not held by git.
shavasana.somatic: Reading this now: is the origin you remember the one the record shows, or does Day 0 for you sit earlier than 471d5739?
shavasana.disposition: RETURN to Zach for the voice read. The other four books wait on it.
